translation:
Middle fullness and bloating-fullness are (also) called drum-distension (guzhang); the four limbs not swollen, the head with no complaint. Navel protruding, sinews (veins) green, small water (scant urine); in men it rises from below, in women from above.
Press it and it does not make a hollow (pit) — a reversed condition; not comparable to many forms of water-swelling. Fenxiao Tang Yin (Separate-and-Drain Beverage) can return the spring; the family-transmitted Zhengqi (Rectify-Qi), who would yield its place?

Fenxiao Tang (Separate-and-Drain Decoction)
Fenxiao Tang (Separate-and-Drain) inside has Fuling (Poria); Cangzhu (Atractylodes), Houpu, Baizhu and Zhi (Zhike) and Sharen. Chenpi, Muxiang (Aucklandia), Xiangfu (Cyperus) and Zexie (Alisma); with Dafupi (Areca Peel) it may even and level.
In this formula, if qi urgent add Chenxiang (Aquilaria); if swollen, add root of radish.

Jiachuan Zhenqi Tang (Family-Transmitted Rectify-Qi Decoction)
The family-transmitted zhenqi, Wuyao (Lindera) is marvelous; Huoxiang (Pogostemon), Xiangfu, Houpu, Zhi (Zhike) and Chenpi. Banxia (Pinellia), Cangzhu (Atractylodes), Dafupi (Areca Peel) and shell; regulating the spleen and resolving distension, letting it gallop freely.
translator_notes: 鼓脹=drum distension; 分消湯=Fenxiao Tang; 家傳正氣湯=Jiachuan Zhengqi Tang.
book: 七十二症辨治方法（手抄本）

translation:
The disease of water-swelling comes from the spleen; the world does not recognize it and guesses wildly. Kidney water and spleen earth both must be steadied; once the spleen earth is depleted, water has no enclosure.
Overflowing and spreading, it flows toward the four limbs, making a person swollen with a yellow sheen. Wind-swelling, qi-swelling, and blood-swelling; yin-water and yang-water also one must know.
Wind-swelling moves and shoots, the skin numb; qi-swelling follows the qi and increases a little with it. How does one recognize the condition of blood-swelling? In the skin, red filaments, traces of blood are seen.
Yang-water naturally hot, yin-water cold; for yin-water none is as marvelous as Weiling (Stomach & Poria). What is feared is that, the road's forks being level and even, or with the addition of qi-panting, the life hangs by a thread.

Muxiang Liuqi San (Aucklandia Flow-Qi Powder)
Muxiang Liuqi (Aucklandia Flow-Qi) with Qing (Qingpi) and Chenpi; Xiangfu (Cyperus), Maimen (Ophiopogon) and Dafupi (Areca Peel). Mugua (Chaenomeles), Mutong (Akebia), Gui (Cinnamon), Renshen (Ginseng), Fuling and Zhu (Atractylodes); Ban (Pinellia), Houpu, Ge (Kudzu/Pueraria), Bing (Binglang/Areca), Guo (Caoguo/Cardamom), Huo (Huoxiang/Pogostemon) and Chen (Chenxiang/Aquilaria).

Shi Pi Yin (Enliven-the-Spleen Beverage)
Shipí (Enliven-the-Spleen) with Zexie (Alisma), Zhuling and Fuling; Cangzhu (Atractylodes), Houpu, Baizhu and Zhi (Zhike) and Sharen. Muxiang (Aucklandia), Xiangfu (Cyperus) and Chenpi together; add Dafupi (Areca Peel), most efficacious.

Bazheng San (Eight-Corrections Powder)
Bazheng (Eight-Corrections) for swelling uses Cheqianzi (Plantago Seed); Qumai (Dianthus), Bianxu (Polygonum aviculare) and Shanzhizi (Gardenia). Huashi (Talc), Mutong (Akebia), prepared Dahuang (Rhubarb); yang-water with body heat may be given it.

Weiling Tang (Stomach-and-Five-Peels Decoction)
Weiling Tang is the name of two decoctions (Pingwei + Wuling); Gancao (Licorice), Chenpi, Houpu and Zhu (Atractylodes) leveling. Add on Baizhu together with Rougui (Cinnamomum cassia); Zhuling, Zexie and Zhu (Zhuling)-Fuling.
translator_notes: 木香流氣散=Muxiang Liuqi San; 實脾飲=Shi Pi Yin; 八正散=Bazheng San; 胃苓湯=Weiling Tang (Pingwei San + Wuling San).
book: 七十二症辨治方法（手抄本）

translation:
Accumulation (ji) is internally yin-blood and governs the formed-body; the five viscera transmit contagiously, not permitting feeling. In the heart it is called Fuliang (tumbling piglet rising toward the heart, 伏梁); in the liver, Feiqi (肥氣, fat-qi); in the spleen it is called Piqi (痞氣, glomus-qi) with metal (lung) suffocating gold.
In the kidney it is Bentun (奔跑/奔豚, running piglet), each dwelling in its parts; since antiquity the five accumulations have a famed name. Mass (ju) is yang qi, being formless (巳/無形); the six bowels over-flowing-healing, touch the scene and thereby form.
Though accumulated, it has no root and stem; to the east it comes, swelling pain, and to the west again. There are further glomus-blocks, the general name hue; zheng, jia, xuan and pi (症瘕痃癖) one must distinguish clearly.
Zheng is tiny and does not move; in the abdomen hard and solid, pain pitiable. Jia is false (假), and can move; at one moment gathering, another dispersing, truly hard to rely upon.
Xuan is at the corner-side like the snap of a finger; frequently it produces pain, hard to stretch out when vomiting. Pi lodges at the flanks and ribs, its form vaguely; though with many thorns-in-twenty, it is a transient form.
Always it is that yin and yang are not harmonious giving rise to it; phlegm, food-stasis, congealed blood are truly its reality. Qipai Tang (Seven-Qi Decoction) with additions and subtractions use; Kuijian Yin (Erode-the-Solid Beverage) then search out again.

Qiqitang (Seven-Qi Decoction)
In the Seven-Qi Decoction use Yizhi (Alpinia oxyphylla); Sanling (Triangular rhizome), Ezhu (Zedoary) and Huoxiang (Pogostemon) lodged within. Qingpi and Chenpi with Gui (Cinnamon) and Jiegeng (Platycodon) added; Xiangfu (Cyperus) and Gancao (Licorice), please taste first.

Kuijian Tang (Erode-the-Solid Decoction)
Inside Kuijian Tang are Zhi (Zhike/Bitter Orange) and Sharen; Banxia (Pinellia), Chenpi and Houpu sought. Xiangfu (Cyperus), Dang Gui, Muxiang (Aucklandia) and Zhu (Atractylodes); when Shanzha (Hawthorn) is used up, all accumulations level flat.
Left flank has a mass, add Chuanxiong; right flank add Qingpi. Meat-food forming a mass, add ginger-juice-stir-fried Huanglian. Powdered-flour food-stasis add Shenqu (Medicated Leaven). Blood mass add Taoren (Peach Kernel), Honghua (Safflower) and Gui, remove Banxia and Shanzha. Phlegm mass add Zhishi (Immature Bitter Orange), Gualou (Trichosanthes) and Haishi, remove Shanzha. Cellular distension add Luobozhi (Radish Seed) and Binglang (Areca), remove Zhu (Baizhu). Stout and healthy persons add Shanzha. Thin persons add a little Renshen.
translator_notes: 五積=the five accumulations (伏梁/肥氣/痞氣/奔豚 etc.); 症瘕痃癖=zheng jia xuan pi (abdominal masses).
七氣湯=Qiqitang; 潰堅湯=Kuijian Tang.
unresolved: "奔豚/奔跑" pun; read as Running-Piglet (Tunti).
book: 七十二症辨治方法（手抄本）
